question: When was the second war between the British army and Burma started?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1852**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Second Anglo-Burmese War started in **1852**.
 
• This conflict was initiated due to disputes over the implementation of the Treaty of Yandabo and British interests in Burma.
 
• The war resulted in the annexation of Pegu, leading to the establishment of British control over Lower Burma.
 
• The war ended in **1853** with the British gaining substantial territorial control.
 
• The annexation significantly impacted the region's political landscape, paving the way for further British expansion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **First Anglo-Burmese War**

 
 
• Lasted from 1824 to 1826.
 
• Concluded with the Treaty of Yandabo, which imposed heavy indemnities on Burma.
 
• Resulted in the cession of territories including Assam, Manipur, Arakan, and Tenasserim to the British.
 
 
 
• **Third Anglo-Burmese War**
 
 
• Occurred in 1885.
 
• Led to the complete annexation of Burma into British India.
 
• Resulted from British commercial interests and the desire to preclude French influence in the region.
 
 
 
• **British Colonial Administration**
 
 
• Burma was administered as a province of British India until 1937.
 
• Post-1937, Burma became a separately administered colony.
 
• British rule significantly impacted Burma's socio-economic structures and cultural landscape.
 
 
 
• **Impact of British Rule**
 
 
• Introduced Western education and legal systems.
 
• Development of infrastructure such as railways and ports.
 
• Economic exploitation and changes in land ownership patterns.
 
• Rise of nationalist movements leading to Burma's independence in 1948.
